newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel plans govt spending freeze in Jan - sources.
newsitem.headline: Waigel plans govt spending freeze in Jan - sources.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel will slap a freeze on extra government spending this month, but no date has been set for its implementation, coalition sources said on Thursday.

A Finance Ministry spokesman contacted separately did not confirm a report in the Bild tabloid that the spending clampdown would be imposed from January 28, when a government annual economic report will be published.
"No decision has yet been taken," the spokesman said.
Bild, in a report based on Finance Ministry sources, said in its Thursday edition that government spending items in excess of 500,000 marks would have to be individually approved.

Waigel wants to bring the total public sector deficit below the Maastricht treaty's target of three percent of gross domestic product this year so that Germany can qualify for European monetary union in 1999.
The overall deficit was 3.9 percent of GDP in 1996. Federal borrowing last year overshot budget targets by 18.4 billion marks to hit 78.3 billion marks, Waigel said on Wednesday.

Wolfgang Weng, budget spokesman for junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), has already called for a spending freeze. Politicians from all German parties fear Waigel's budget arithmetic could come under pressure from post-war record unemployment, forcing higher-than-planned spending on jobless benefits.
